# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33 (Bi-Vb Pc33)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc33
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33
**Title (English, from literature):** Making a nun ill at ease
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33 (*Aphāsukaraṇa*) is a Vinaya training rule governing the conduct of Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunī*s). According to the rule, a nun who intentionally causes discomfort, annoyance, or vexation to another nun commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In the framing narrative of the text, the rule is prompted by an incident involving the nun Thullanandā [Hüsken 1997]. Because the rule is formulated in broad terms, subsequent Vinaya regulations serve as specific instances of this prohibition [Hüsken 1997]. In its exoneration clause (*anāpatti*), the only ground for exemption from an offense is if the perpetrator acts without the deliberate intention to cause trouble or discomfort to another [Hüsken 1997].

  An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
